variables.claim_asserts: Islands more than 300 miles from a continent or great continental island have no native non-flying terrestrial mammals.
variables.test_measures: GBIF occurrences of non-bat, non-marine, non-human mammals in 43 island units farther than 300 miles from Natural Earth landmasses of at least 100,000 square kilometres, using at least 10 records and at least 95% inside-unit as an endemism proxy for nativeness.

modality.note: GBIF occurrence records fit island mammal presence, while near-endemism conservatively proxies native status and Natural Earth geometry operationalizes distance.

assumptions.note: The exclusions track non-flying terrestrial mammals; 100,000 square kilometres is a declared proxy for Darwin's 'great continental island,' and representative-point distances approximate island-to-land distance.

scope.claim_scope: Any island more than 300 miles from a continent or great continental island.
scope.test_scope: Forty-three pre-registered far-island units under an area-based great-island definition, detecting only mammals satisfying a conservative endemism threshold.

reasons: Five endemic Galápagos rice rats on an island unit 1068.4 kilometres from qualifying land directly address the asserted variables.
The interpretation declares the endemism rule, 100,000-square-kilometre great-island proxy, and representative-point distance method.
The finite island sample and proxy definitions narrow the universal geographic scope, despite supplying relevant counterexamples.
what_would_change_it: Use a comprehensive island inventory, minimum coastline-to-coastline distances, a historically justified definition of great continental island, and authoritative native-status records rather than endemism alone.
